The MS_WAIT field shall be a fullword integer (4 bytes) designed to store a wait time ranging from 1 millisecond to 900 milliseconds.
The software shall consider the DFHEISTG data structure as the end of a dynamic storage area.
The software shall recognize a constant named CACBAR, which is equivalent to the numeric value 12, indicating the beginning of a DFHCOMMAREA from the requesting program.

The specification must accommodate the presence of a DFHCOMMAREA from the requesting program, as indicated by the CACBAR constant, though the exact structure and content of this DFHCOMMAREA are not specified within the provided code snippet.

Testing for the CACBAR constant shall verify that it is recognized by the software as indicating the beginning of a DFHCOMMAREA and that it has been assigned a numeric value of 12.

The software requirements specification document must acknowledge areas where the code's functionality is not completely specified, such as the absence of detailed operations for the DFHEISTG structure or the contents and structure of the DFHCOMMAREA, and note these as areas for further clarification.

The first field within DFHCA, named CA_RC, shall be a character string with a length of 4 bytes and is designated to contain a return code.

The second field within DFHCA, named CA_WAIT, shall be a fullword (4 bytes) integer value that specifies a wait time. The valid range for CA_WAIT is from 1 to 90, representing 10ms to 900ms increments respectively.

To test the functionality of the DFHCA data structure, a test suite shall be developed that verifies each field can be correctly initialized, accessed, and modified according to the specifications. L8WAIT   DFHEIENT CODEREG=(2),DATAREG=10,EIBREG=11
L8WAIT   AMODE 31
L8WAIT   RMODE ANY
         B     SYSDATE                 BRANCH AROUND LITERALS
         DC    CL08'L8WAIT  '
         DC    CL48' -- z/OS STIMERM running on an L8 TCB  '
         DC    CL08'        '
         DC    CL08'&SYSDATE'
         DC    CL08'        '
         DC    CL08'&SYSTIME'
SYSDATE  DS   0H
***********************************************************************
* ENTER TRACENUM before STIMERM                                       *
***********************************************************************
SY_0010  DS   0H
         EXEC CICS ENTER TRACENUM(T_35)                                X
              FROM(T_35_M)                                             X
              FROMLENGTH(T_LEN)                                        X
              RESOURCE(T_RES)                                          X
              NOHANDLE
***********************************************************************
* Address DFHCOMMAREA.  If not present, use 2.5 millisecond default.  *
***********************************************************************
SY_0020  DS   0H
         LA    R1,CA_LEN               Load DSECT length
         LH    R15,EIBCALEN            Load DFHCOMMAREA length
         CR    R1,R15                  Valid length?
         BC    B'0111',SY_0800         ... no,  use 2.5ms default
         L     R12,DFHEICAP            Load DFHCOMMAREA
         USING DFHCA,R12               ... tell assembler
***********************************************************************
* The valid range accepted is 1, which equates to 10 milliseconds     *
* thru 90, which equates to 900 milliseconds.  Any value less than 1  *
* will be set to 1 and any value greater than 90 will be set to 90.   *
***********************************************************************
SY_0030  DS   0H
         MVC   CA_RC,RC_0001           Set RC for default
         MVC   MS_WAIT,=F'1'           Set default 10 milliseconds
         CLC   CA_WAIT,=F'0'           Zero or less?
         BC    B'1100',SY_0100         ... yes, use 10ms default
         MVC   CA_RC,RC_0090           Set RC for default
         MVC   MS_WAIT,=F'90'          Set maximum 900 milliseconds
         CLC   CA_WAIT,=F'90'          Greater than 900 milliseconds?
         BC    B'0011',SY_0100         ... yes, use 900ms default
         MVC   MS_WAIT,CA_WAIT         Use requested interval
         MVC   CA_RC,RC_0000           Set RC for requested wait
***********************************************************************
* Issue z/OS STIMERM.                                                 *
* Using fullword binary value of 1 (10ms) thru 90 (900ms)             *
***********************************************************************
SY_0100  DS   0H
         LA   R3,STIMERID              Load STIMER ID
         LA   R4,MS_WAIT               Load wait time
         STIMERM SET,BINTVL=(R4),WAIT=YES,ID=(R3)
         BC   B'1111',SY_0900          Exit trace
***********************************************************************
* Issue z/OS STIMERM.                                                 *
* 2.5 milliseconds (2500 microseconds)                                *
***********************************************************************
SY_0800  DS   0H
         LA   R3,STIMERID              Load STIMER ID
         STIMERM SET,MICVL=MIC2500,WAIT=YES,ID=(R3)
***********************************************************************
* ENTER TRACE after  STIMERM                                          *
***********************************************************************
SY_0900  DS   0H
*
         EXEC CICS ENTER TRACENUM(T_46)                                X
              FROM(T_46_M)                                             X
              FROMLENGTH(T_LEN)                                        X
              RESOURCE(T_RES)                                          X
              NOHANDLE
***********************************************************************
* Return to calling program                                           *
***********************************************************************
RETURN   DS   0H
         EXEC CICS RETURN
***********************************************************************
* Literal Pool                                                        *
***********************************************************************
         LTORG
*
RC_0001  DC    CL04'0010'              Default RC for  10MS
RC_0090  DC    CL04'0900'              Default RC for 900MS
RC_0000  DC    CL04'0000'              Default RC for requested wait
*
T_35     DC    H'35'                   TRACE number  before STIMERM
T_46     DC    H'46'                   TRACE number  after  STIMERM
T_35_M   DC    CL08'GoodNite'          TRACE message before STIMERM
T_46_M   DC    CL08'Wake-Up!'          TRACE message after  STIMERM
T_RES    DC    CL08'L8WAIT    '        TRACE resource
T_LEN    DC    H'08'                   TRACE message length
         DS   0D
MIC0256  DC    F'0'                    1st word
         DC    F'01048576'             0.2 milliseconds
         DS   0D
MIC1024  DC    F'0'                    1st word
         DC    F'04194304'             1.0 milliseconds
         DS   0D
MIC2500  DC    F'0'                    1st word
         DC    F'10240000'             2.5 milliseconds
         DS   0F
R0       EQU   0
R1       EQU   1
R2       EQU   2
R3       EQU   3
R4       EQU   4
R5       EQU   5
R6       EQU   6
R7       EQU   7
R8       EQU   8
R9       EQU   9
R10      EQU   10
R11      EQU   11
R12      EQU   12
R13      EQU   13
R14      EQU   14
R15      EQU   15
*
***********************************************************************
* End of Program                                                      *
***********************************************************************
         END   L8WAIT
requirements: The software shall initialize with a default code and data register setup, specifically setting the code register to 2 and the data register to 10.
The software shall operate in AMODE 31 and RMODE ANY, ensuring compatibility across various operating modes and memory models.
The software must provide a branch operation to bypass literals, ensuring efficient execution flow and memory use.
The software shall support entering trace numbers before and after executing a specified timer operation, utilizing CICS commands with predefined trace numbers, messages, and resource identifiers.
The software must handle DFHCOMMAREA (Communication Area) by checking its presence and validity. If invalid or absent, a 2.5 millisecond default wait time is used.

The software shall validate and normalize input wait times, converting a range of 1 to 90 into corresponding wait times from 10 milliseconds to 900 milliseconds. Any input outside this range shall be adjusted to the nearest limit within it.
The software must issue a z/OS STIMERM command with either a binary interval value for wait times within the valid range or a fixed 2.5 milliseconds wait time when the default is applied.

Upon completion of the timer operation, the software shall enter a trace number to mark the end of the wait period, utilizing CICS commands with a predefined trace number, message, and resource identifier.
The software must properly return control to the calling program following the execution of its main functionality, including timer wait and trace number logging.

The software shall include a defined literal pool at the end of the program for organizational and reference purposes, containing default return codes, trace numbers, messages, and a microsecond value for the 2.5 milliseconds default wait time.
The software must be tested for its ability to properly interpret and handle DFHCOMMAREA input, including cases where it is absent, valid, or invalid.

Test cases shall include validating the proper adjustment and application of wait times based on input values, ensuring that values outside the range of 1 to 90 are correctly adjusted to 10 milliseconds or 900 milliseconds as appropriate.

The functionality to issue a z/OS STIMERM command with specified wait times must be tested to verify that the software correctly translates input values into appropriate timer intervals and handles the default 2.5 milliseconds wait time correctly.

Trace entry functionality before and after the timer wait must be tested to ensure that the software correctly logs the predefined trace numbers and messages, indicating the start and end of the wait period.
